page: Microsoft Azure E96a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7452 processor. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at up to 3.35 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware instruction support for AES, SHA-NI, AVX, BMI2, and FMA. It does not include AVX-512 or AMX extensions.

Memory capacity is configured at 672.0 GB of RAM, equating to 7.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark results indicate solid caching efficiency, with small-block cached read bandwidth reaching 3932.23 GB/sec in the top 25% bracket, while uncached 256MB read and write bandwidth settle at 162.3 GB/sec and 79.33 GB/sec. The instance includes 2577 GB of local SSD storage, while accelerator hardware is absent with zero GPUs, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Computational benchmarks demonstrate a divergence between single-threaded and parallelized throughput. The stress-ng single-core result registers in the bottom 10%, yet parallel throughput yields a PassMark CPU score of 68394.35 and an encryption score of 97050.01 in the top 10%. Multi-threaded data processing remains effective, highlighted by 408.55 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 71.0 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, large-model LLM prompt processing is constrained, managing 5.04 tokens per second.

With its dense 672.0 GB memory footprint, integrated 2.5 TB SSD storage, and 96 vCPUs, the E96a_v4 is technically tailored for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes, memory-intensive data analytics, and high-concurrency enterprise applications that depend on vast memory capacity rather than peak single-core execution speed.
description: Microsoft Azure E96a_v4 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs and 48 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7452 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.35 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 672.0 GB of RAM (7.0 GB per core) and bundled 2577 GB local SSD storage without GPU acceleration. The hardware configuration emphasizes parallel data throughput, supported by top-tier cryptographic acceleration and strong cached memory bandwidth of 3932.23 GB/sec. Benchmarks reflect moderate single-core performance alongside strong multi-threaded capabilities, including 71.0 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark CPU score of 68394.35. The server is well suited for memory-bound workloads, such as extensive in-memory caches, relational database systems, and large analytics engines requiring substantial RAM and multi-core concurrency.
